observations.selection: One colony with WS morphology per independent culture; mixtures of genetic backgrounds include pathway double deletions.
observations.truth_procedure: Candidate-gene Sanger sequencing; genome sequencing for a few candidates without identified focal mutations.
observations.interpretation: Concrete non-focal biological routes occur within the selected WS-mutant collection. This conditional sample composition is not a false-entry probability for known-Other units.

observations.anchor: SWS: a wsp-, aws-, and mws-independent route to WS
observations.interpretation: A WS phenotype can occur despite deletion of the three focal modules. Functional swsR dependence was demonstrated, while repeated sequencing did not identify its causal mutation. A selected strain and its suppressor mutants are not independent known-Other eligibility trials.

anchors: Table 1 WSX row and footnote b
observations.interpretation: WSX lacks an identified mutation in the focal loci but depends functionally on Wsp; molecular uncertainty does not establish known-Other truth. Suppressor insertions are mechanistic observations, not independent negative-control trials.

conclusion: The inspected sources establish that a WS phenotype gate can admit non-focal routes; they do not supply a known-Other pre-gate denominator and independent frozen-gate outcome ledger for numerical native false-entry calibration.
